text:
Imran Shafiq, a salaried medical sales officer, opened his Karachi account in July 2021 and declares a monthly income of PKR 150,000. Beginning on 2 June 2026 the account received a series of cash deposits ranging from PKR 1.5 million to PKR 2.0 million, each just under the statutory cash‑transaction reporting (CTR) threshold of PKR 2 million. The deposits were made at four different branches (Clifton, Saddar, DHA‑Phase 6) on almost every day of the month, totalling more than PKR 30 million in cash within 30 days. The customer declined to explain the source of the cash when asked by branch staff on 14 June and refused to complete the extra paperwork required for large cash deposits.  

During the same period the account transferred large sums to “Crescent Imports” – PKR 4.6 million on 5 June, PKR 4.5 million on 10 June, PKR 5.4 million on 15 June, PKR 3.3 million on 20 June, PKR 5.7 million on 25 June and PKR 2.8 million on 30 June – all via IBFT or RTGS to the same counterparties at synthetic banks. The pattern shows repeated structuring of cash inflows just below the CTR limit, rapid consolidation of those funds, and immediate high‑value outflows to a single business partner, which is inconsistent with the customer’s declared salary and occupation.  

These behaviours trigger the STR‑PK‑01 typology (score 320 > alert threshold 300) for repeated cash deposits within 20 % below the CTR threshold and cross‑branch activity. The combination of unexplained large cash deposits, refusal to provide source information, and swift large transfers to the same counterparty constitutes a strong suspicion of money‑laundering and warrants filing a Suspicious Transaction Report.
